class.name: SpriteStudioAudioBackend
class.brief_description: Routes a [SpriteStudioPlayer2D]'s audio events to something other than the built-in player.
class.description:
By default [SpriteStudioPlayer2D] plays the sounds authored on audio parts through its own pooled [AudioStreamPlayer] voices. Assign a subclass of this resource to [member SpriteStudioPlayer2D.audio_backend] to take that over - for audio middleware, for a bus/attenuation setup of your own, or to keep every sound under one mixer. Assigning a backend always suppresses the built-in playback, including [member SpriteStudioPlayer2D.audio_volume], so the backend fully owns voice lifecycle and play counts. It is invoked only while playback runs forward: reverse playback fires no audio at all, which is a runtime-wide limitation rather than a backend one. Subclass it in GDScript (or C++) and override [method play_audio]: [codeblock] # res://audio/my_backend.gd extends SpriteStudioAudioBackend
func play_audio(payload: Dictionary, ssab: SSABResource, player: Node) -> void: var info := ssab.get_sound_info(payload["sound_list_name_hash"], payload["sound_name_hash"]) if info.is_empty(): return # Hand info["path"] and payload["loop_num"] to your own audio stack. MyMiddleware.play(info["path"], payload["loop_num"]) [/codeblock] Save the script as a resource ([code].tres[/code], or a [code].gd[/code] assigned in the inspector) and drop it on the player's [b]Audio Backend[/b] property. One backend resource can be shared by any number of players - the originating node arrives as the [code]player[/code] argument.

method.name: play_audio
method.description: Called once per audio event the player passes while playing forward. [param payload] is the same dictionary [signal SpriteStudioPlayer2D.audio] carries ([code]part_index[/code], [code]part_name[/code], [code]frame_no[/code], [code]sound_list_name_hash[/code], [code]sound_name_hash[/code], [code]sound_name[/code], [code]loop_num[/code]). [param ssab] is the resource the sound was authored in - use [method SSABResource.get_sound_info] or [method SSABResource.get_sound_stream] to resolve it - and [param player] is the [SpriteStudioPlayer2D] that fired it. The default implementation does nothing, so a backend that only wants to observe some events still silences the rest.
